answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with licensed community garden plots: each identity tends one real plot in a shared garden watered by a karst spring, its founding fable and harvest log kept public by an independent warden. Random spot-checks summon the holder to weed their own plot within a day, and one person cannot tend two distant plots at once. The plot fee in outside money doubles per further identity on the same funding trail, so every extra fake costs another real garden, another season of tending, another human, and twice the prior fee.
